method: Deterministic summary of computed figures. No language model is used.
national: One Nation led national search interest in the week to 24 November, averaging 46.4 on Google's 0-100 scale, 4.3 times the next party (the Greens). That is 65% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
One Nation rose the most on the previous week, up 15.7 points (+51%).
Searches for the Greens jumped to 11 on 20 November, 2.1 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “Hadley: Stop Greens’ Aboriginal identity rort now” (The Daily Telegraph).
victoria: Across the latest poll from each of 7 pollsters, the Coalition averages 31.9% of the primary vote, Labor 21.4%, One Nation 22.6% and the Greens 14.3%. On two-party-preferred the Coalition leads 57.5 to 42.5 (6 polls), a 12.5-point swing to the Coalition since 2022.
Applied uniformly to the 2022 pendulum, that swing points to a Coalition majority (66 seats, 45 needed). Treat this as the classic two-party read only: it cannot see One Nation winning seats.
The Roy Morgan MRP (March 2026 - September 2026), which models seats one by one, projects Coalition 62, Labor 40, One Nation 11 and Greens 6: a majority.
Preferred premier (Resolve, 20–23 Nov 2026): Wilson 34%, Carroll 23%, Pickering 19%.
